answer.diagnosis: The model appears to use overall image brightness, most likely background brightness, as a shortcut. The evidence is layer-1 unit 19. Every one of its 576 weights is positive (about +1 to +91, mean about 50). Its grid has no centre/surround structure and weights the far corners and border as much as the centre. By contrast, the size-tuned units have clear radial structure. Units 1, 6, 9, 11, 12, 16, 27 and 30 respond to a ring or disk around the centre. Units 0, 3, 5, 8, 14, 15, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25, 28 and 31 have the opposite centre/surround pattern. The remaining units look like zero-mean noise. A detector driven only by blob size would focus on the centre region. A flat, all-positive filter means the classes differed in brightness across the whole frame. Unit 19 is also large in effect: its summed real weight is about 41 per unit of mean pixel intensity. A small change in background level therefore shifts it by several units, which is more than the blob-size difference adds. It feeds most layer-2 units with sizeable weights (u13 +69, u15 +68, u12 +43, u9 +39, u14 +37, u0 +36). Fix: remove unit 19's dependence on pixel values and replace it with a constant near its typical activation. This is a guessed value (mean pixel about 0.25), not derived from the weights, so calibration downstream may be off. The size-tuned units are left unchanged.

edits.reason: keep its typical activation as a constant for calibration
